report.rationale: Normal polarity leaves the three measured physical bits at 0. Actuator stiction is the only candidate compatible with all three disclosed mappings. Each nearest alternative conflicts with one physical bit. E10 corroborates bit 3 but is a correlated repeat, not independent confirmation. E14 and the independent audit E18 identify the estimator as stale, so cached outputs should not override the physical evidence. Residual uncertainty reflects possible measurement or mapping error.

Normal polarity (E11) preserves the measured zeros. Actuator stiction is the sole candidate compatible with E15, E09, and E03 together. Sensor bias conflicts with E15, none_of_the_above with E09, circulation loss with E03, and controller timing fault with all three. E10 is a correlated repeat, not independent confirmation. E14 and E18 establish estimator staleness, not invalidity of the physical measurements. The diagnosis survives review, but numerical probabilities remain judgmental because priors and measurement-error rates are unspecified. Circulation loss is tied with sensor bias and none_of_the_above as the nearest alternative. Recommended repeats could check reproducibility but cannot independently exclude systematic error.
